subject: Resilience buffer, uptime threshold and monthly remedy outline
messages_1_subject: Initial ask: tightened uptime for pilot & credit mechanics
messages_1_body:
Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo — the team liked the performance profile. As we prepare procurement, two quick asks from my side so I can move this to legal and finance: 

1) For the pilot (Q3, ~$35k/month) CloudHaven needs an uptime commitment of 99.995% for the dedicated pool serving our latency-sensitive endpoints.
2) We need clarity on the monthly remedy: specifically how credits are calculated for partial-day degradations and any cap relative to committed spend.

We can be flexible on form, but procurement wants an explicit example table showing uptime bands -> % credit -> payout timing. Also, can Redwood accommodate a one-time maintenance carveout during our weekend migration (target: 6/21–6/22) without that window counting toward credits?

I've attached the procurement term sheet to help. Can we get a counterproposal by end of next week?

Best,
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Operations
CloudHaven Inc.

Attachment: CloudHaven_Procurement_Termsheet.xlsx
messages_2_subject: Re: Initial ask: tightened uptime for pilot & credit mechanics
messages_2_body:
Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear asks and the term sheet.

High level response: we can propose a narrow "resilience buffer" approach for pilots that blends a tighter uptime promise with a staged remedy ladder rather than an uncapped monthly payout. Key points below and I'll loop legal for contract language: 

- Uptime: For the dedicated pilot pool we can offer 99.995% for the pilot duration, conditional on a small resilience buffer (we call it a 30-minute monthly buffer) that excludes up to 30 cumulative minutes of minor interruptions before credits trigger. The buffer acknowledges transient infra noise during ramp.

- Remedy ladder (example):
  * >=99.995% — no credits
  * 99.99%–99.994% — 5% of monthly invoice credited
  * 99.9%–99.989% — 15% credited
  * <99.9% — 40% credited, with a hard cap at 100% of monthly committed spend.

- Partial-day calculation: credits will be prorated by minutes of service impact within the month, with the resilience buffer applied first.

- Maintenance carveout: we can grant a one-time maintenance carveout for your migration window (6/21–6/22) if the window is scheduled and jointly confirmed 14 days in advance; that window will be excluded from monthly uptime calculations.

I attached a concise counterproposal that mirrors the above and includes examples. Laura — tagging you for any legal/contract concerns. Sean/Marissa — wanted you on this for deal economics.

Will get a formal PDF back to you by EOW (Friday).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Counterproposal_20250418.pdf
messages_3_subject: Re: Initial ask: tightened uptime for pilot & credit mechanics
messages_3_body:
Thanks — short legal notes from my side: 

1) Resilience buffer: we should call this an "Operational Graceband" in contract language and define it as cumulative, not continuous, minutes per calendar month. Also add a clause that excludes customer-initiated platform tests that are documented in advance.

2) Remedy ladder: the hard cap at 100% of committed monthly spend is acceptable. For the 40% band below 99.9%, propose adding an alternative remedy option — a service credit or an agreed remediation plan + partial credit — to give us operational flexibility. 

3) Maintenance carveout: the one-time exclusion is fine but add a mutual notification clause (14 days) and that Redwood will provide a post-maintenance operations summary within 48 hours. 

4) Auditability: CloudHaven asked about how credits are computed. We'll include an appendix with a worked example table and a link to the monthly availability report (read-only) generated from our monitoring. If CloudHaven needs access to raw telemetry, that will be scoped as a separate SOW.

If those bullets look ok, I'll prepare a short contract amendment and send it to Aisha for signature.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
messages_4_subject: Re: Initial ask: tightened uptime for pilot & credit mechanics
messages_4_body:
Hi Aisha — quick commercial note: we won't insist on a separate escrowing mechanism for credits for a pilot of this size. The cap at 100% of monthly committed spend keeps risk bounded.

Also, Marissa will follow up on pricing: tightening SLA to 99.995% pushes the pilot tier to a small premium (roughly +12% on monthly committed spend) because it requires reserved capacity and additional redundancy. If that's acceptable, we'll reflect the uplift in the order form.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
messages_5_subject: Re: Initial ask: tightened uptime for pilot & credit mechanics
messages_5_body:
Thanks everyone — that readout is helpful and aligns with our procurement expectations. A few follow-ups: 

- The resilience buffer concept is acceptable to leadership as long as the appendix has the minute-level worked example we discussed.
- Confirming the migration carveout process — we'll send the maintenance notice by 2025-06-07 and expect the post-maintenance summary within 48 hours.
- Price uplift: I can take the +12% premium to Finance for approval; please send an updated order form with the uplifted line and the SLA amendment.

If we can get the amendment + order form this week, I'll route it internally next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Aisha
